title: Component Patterns Core Check
description: Check your understanding of composition, HOCs, render props, compound components, and container patterns.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does React composition usually prefer over inheritance?

options.text: Combining components with props, children, and small APIs

questions.explanation: React favors composing behavior and UI through component relationships rather than inheritance hierarchies.

options.text: A function that takes a component and returns an enhanced component
A component with more than one div
A hook that returns JSX only

questions.explanation: An HOC wraps a component to share behavior or inject props.

options.text: A prop that is a function used to decide what UI to render
The key prop on a list

questions.explanation: Render props pass rendering control to the caller through a function.

questions.prompt: Which are composition techniques covered in this module? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: children, slot props, and compound components are common React composition APIs.

questions.prompt: What is the idea behind compound components?

options.text: Related components coordinate behind a shared parent API
Every component must be wrapped in React.memo
Components inherit methods from each other
State is stored only in URLs

questions.explanation: Compound components let callers compose related pieces while the parent manages shared behavior.

questions.prompt: What does the container/presentational split separate?

options.text: Data and behavior from display-focused UI

questions.explanation: Containers manage data and behavior; presentational components focus on rendering props.

questions.prompt: Controlled components receive their current value and change handler from outside.
questions.explanation: Controlled APIs put state ownership in the parent or caller.

questions.prompt: What is a common HOC pitfall?

options.text: Prop name collisions with the wrapped component

questions.explanation: HOCs can accidentally override or collide with props expected by the wrapped component.
